review_notes: I read the whole target file and the definitions it uses: `Node`, `step`, `terminal`, `terminal_nil` and `terminal_cons` in PrimeRatioBins.lean, and `Side.flip` in FiniteHistorySupport.lean. I grepped the Jacobsthal tree for uses of `terminal_gap_sum`, `simp [..step..Side.flip]` and `change (step ..)`. I found no `step_side`, `step_gap`, `step_cutoff` or `step_ratio` lemmas, and no simp lemmas for `Side.flip`. I did not run Lean. The suggested lemmas are untested, and I could not check whether the new simp rules would change the outcome of any existing `simp` call elsewhere in the tree. The statement of `terminal_gap_sum` is fine and the proofs are otherwise unaffected.

findings.problem: `step` has no simp lemmas for its fields (`side`, `gap`, `cutoff`, `ratio`), so projections of `step w z p` cannot be simplified. The proof of `terminal_gap_sum` falls back on a `change` that restates the unfolded `gap` field. Line 51 does `simp [terminal,step,hi,Side.flip]`, which unfolds the whole definition. `Side.flip` is also unfolded by hand with no simp lemmas for `.even` and `.odd`. The same unfold-by-hand pattern recurs in other files, for example `simp [step,hi,Side.flip]` in ReferenceSourceDecomposition, LatePrimeRatio, StrongReferenceTransport and ActualTagFreezing, and `change (step w z p).ratio-1 ≤ ...` in LatePrimeRatio.
findings.proposed_change: Next to `step` in PrimeRatioBins.lean, add `@[simp] theorem step_side : (step w z p).side = z.side.flip := rfl`, plus `step_gap : (step w z p).gap = z.gap - primeExponent w p`, `step_cutoff` and `step_ratio` in the same form. Also add `@[simp] Side.flip_even : Side.even.flip = Side.odd` and `Side.flip_odd`. Then the `change` in `terminal_gap_sum` becomes `simp [step_gap]; ring` or similar, and line 51 becomes `by simp [terminal, hi]`. The same lemmas replace the repeated `simp [step,hi,Side.flip]` calls and the `change` lines elsewhere.
findings.benefit: The projections of `step` get a canonical normal form. Proofs no longer unfold `step` or rely on `change` to expose the structure fields. Call sites become shorter and do not break if the definition of `step` or `Side.flip` is later refactored.

evidence.excerpt: have hside : (step w z p).side=.odd := by simp [step,hi,Side.flip]

findings.excerpt: theorem terminal_gap_sum (w : ℝ) (z : Node) (ps : List ℕ) :
findings.problem: `terminal_nil` and `terminal_cons` are `@[simp]`, but the closed form `(terminal w z ps).gap = z.gap - (ps.map (primeExponent w)).sum` is not simp, so it is never applied by simp. Every caller uses an explicit `rw [terminal_gap_sum]`, e.g. in this file's `representativeGap_le_actual`, in PrimeBinRepresentatives, PrimeProductLogCoordinates and WordIntervalGeometry, and as `exact terminal_gap_sum w _ _` in CandidateExceptionMass. For a symbolic word `ps`, simp leaves `(terminal w z ps).gap` stuck, while for a concrete cons-list it unfolds through `terminal_cons` and `step`.
findings.proposed_change: Once `step_gap` exists (see the first finding), mark `terminal_gap_sum` `@[simp]`. There is no loop: the right-hand side contains no `terminal`. It also agrees with `terminal_cons` on explicit lists, because simp rewrites the inner `terminal w z (p::ps)` first and the resulting `terminal w (step w z p) ps` then matches `terminal_gap_sum`. The result has the same normal form as unfolding the cons by hand. Alternatively, keep it non-simp and document that `rw` is the intended interface.
findings.benefit: Gap goals about terminal nodes then normalize to `z.gap - sum` without a manual `rw`. This also removes the asymmetry with `terminal_nil` and `terminal_cons`. The residual risk is a changed normal form in other files that use `simp` on `(terminal ...).gap`, which I did not check.

evidence.excerpt: terminal w z (p::ps) = terminal w (step w z p) ps := rfl
